html:
A vote on 9 May 1956, held by the United Nations, in which British Togoland chose to join the Gold Coast, which became independent as Ghana a year later.

The territory was the western part of German Togoland, run by Britain since the First World War. The north voted strongly for union. Many in the south, mostly Ewe, voted against, hoping instead to unite with French Togoland, but the overall majority was for union. Ghana gained what is now the Volta region and much of its north east. The Ewe were left divided between Ghana and Togo, and some still call for unity. See also Ghana's independence.
sum: A vote on 9 May 1956, held by the United Nations, in which British Togoland chose to join the Gold Coast, which became independent as Ghana a year later.
